name: Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM)

location.region: Greater Cairo, adjacent to the Giza Plateau

historical_description: The Grand Egyptian Museum is the world's largest archaeological museum dedicated to a single civilization. Positioned roughly two kilometers from the Giza Pyramids, it was built to consolidate and modernize Egypt's antiquities display, relieving the historic Egyptian Museum in Tahrir Square, and to give the complete Tutankhamun collection a single dedicated home for the first time since its 1922 discovery. Planning began in the early 2000s, with construction starting in 2005; the project faced repeated delays due to funding, political instability (including the 2011 revolution), and the COVID-19 pandemic. Partial/trial openings occurred through 2024, and the museum held its full public grand opening on November 4, 2025.

construction_details.architect: Heneghan Peng Architects (Irish firm, selected via international competition in 2003)
construction_details.site_area: approximately 490,000 square meters, including gardens and conservation facilities
construction_details.notable_design_feature: A triangular glass facade echoing the geometry of the pyramids, aligned so that galleries offer direct sightlines to the Giza Plateau
construction_details.artifact_count: Over 100,000 artifacts spanning roughly 7,000 years of Egyptian history

dynasty: Not applicable (modern institution); houses artifacts spanning prehistoric Egypt through the Greco-Roman period

opening_hours.typical_hours: 09:00–19:00 (hours and days can vary seasonally; night hours sometimes extended for peak season)
opening_hours.closed_days: Varies by season; check official channels before visiting
opening_hours.booking_requirement: Timed, date-specific entry tickets must be booked in advance online; walk-up/on-site ticket sales are generally not available

ticket_price.notes: Prices rose significantly after the November 2025 full opening compared to earlier soft-opening rates (some older sources cite EGP 500-600, which are outdated). Tickets are sold only through the official portal (visit-gem.com) and are non-refundable and non-transferable once booked. Beware of unofficial or fraudulent ticketing websites.

best_visiting_time.time_of_day: Morning slots are less crowded; late-afternoon slots allow combining with sunset views of the pyramids from museum terraces
best_visiting_time.season: Year-round (indoor, climate-controlled), though cooler months (October–April) pair better with an outdoor pyramid visit the same day
best_visiting_time.duration_recommended: 3 to 6 hours depending on depth of interest

interesting_facts: The Grand Egyptian Museum is the largest museum in the world devoted to a single ancient civilization.
It displays the complete Tutankhamun collection (over 5,000 objects) together in one place for the first time since the tomb's 1922 discovery.
The museum houses Khufu's Solar Boat, a full-size cedar funerary vessel over 4,500 years old, in a dedicated hall.
A monumental 11-meter, 83-tonne statue of Ramesses II greets visitors in the Grand Staircase/atrium.
The museum's glass facade and site orientation were deliberately designed to frame direct views of the Giza Pyramids from inside the galleries.
Construction and planning of the museum spanned roughly two decades, making it one of the longest museum development projects in modern history.
related_places: Egyptian Museum, Tahrir Square (older museum, still operating with reduced collection)
unesco_status: Not independently UNESCO-listed, but located within the buffer zone of the Giza Pyramids UNESCO World Heritage Site
accessibility_notes: Fully modern facility with elevators, ramps, and wheelchair accessibility throughout galleries and public areas.
nearest_airport: Cairo International Airport (CAI), approx. 35–45 km away
